requirements.requirement: node1 provides /srv/nfs/shared as an NFSv4 export to node2 and node3 over the dedicated storage network.
requirements.summary: All nodes use 10.100.222.0/24 storage addresses. node1's NFS service is active and enabled, answers NFSv4 RPC requests, and exports the requested path read-write only to the two client addresses. This remained healthy after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 mount node1:/srv/nfs/shared at /mnt/shared.
requirements.summary: Both clients show live NFSv4.2 mounts from 10.100.222.10 at /mnt/shared and persistent fstab entries. The mounts and shared data recovered after each client restart and the later server restart.

requirements.requirement: sharedops has UID and GID 4200 on all three nodes, and the shared directory is sharedops:sharedops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: Direct identity records show UID/GID 4200 on every node. Server and client-side observations show the shared directory owned by 4200:4200/sharedops:sharedops with mode 2770, including after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either client are immediately visible from the other while retaining ownership and permissions.
requirements.summary: Files created as sharedops on node2 and node3 were read directly from the opposite client without a synchronization step. Numeric ownership remained 4200:4200 and modes remained 0640 and 0660. Fresh post-restart files repeated the behavior in both directions.

overall_summary: All material public-task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end evidence. The supplemental node-restart protocol is also complete for every managed node: each has a healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service or mount, identity, and data state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities agree with the executor observations. Restart persistence was treated as corroborating evidence rather than an added public requirement.
limitations: The final lifecycle temporary-file observations inventory /tmp but not /var/tmp, so they cannot independently confirm whether the install helper logs and PID files created by cmd-fc10d768e2c34836, cmd-86268e34c97c464d, and cmd-4fb70d1f955442a0 remained.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated or unnecessary mutation was identified. Package operations established prerequisites; identity, export, service, fstab, directory, and mount changes implemented the task; test-file creation was bounded functional evidence; and restarts served the mandatory provider protocol. The failed root read still created the node2 probe subsequently used, while other failures were read-only discovery or expected reboot disconnects. All nodes finished with consistent package state and no failed services. Minor deduction: the asynchronous install commands created /var/tmp/nfs-install.log and nfs-install.pid on each node. These supported installation polling, but no cleanup was captured; they were not shown reverted and their final presence is indeterminate because lifecycle collection covered /tmp rather than /var/tmp.
